title: The over-privileged analyst — question explanation
learningObjective: Apply least privilege, segregation of duties and timely access review
format: 16:9 educational motion-graphics video; narration; separate captions; no autoplay with sound
visualStyle: Deep navy and charcoal; restrained cyan/electric-blue highlights; limited purple accents; clean typography; purposeful, low-motion transitions; accessible contrast.

scenes.name: Scenario setup
scenes.visual: A data analyst has permanent administrator access to payroll, identity management and production infrastructure, although their role only requires read-only access to one reporting dataset.
scenes.direction: Show a fictional simulated setting. Use generic UI and no actual organization, brand, user identity, credential, real URL or live account.

scenes.name: Learning objective and risk cue
scenes.visual: Apply least privilege, segregation of duties and timely access review
scenes.direction: Highlight only observable cues and explain the decision context without implying certainty beyond the scenario.

scenes.name: Recommended response
scenes.visual: Option B: Remove unnecessary privileges, grant a named read-only role for the required dataset and review access periodically. Access should be limited to the minimum necessary resources and authorizations for assigned tasks.
scenes.direction: Animate the recommended defensive choice as a clear decision path. Display the action verb and trusted channel/control.

scenes.name: Why the other options fail
scenes.visual: Option A: Shared privileged accounts reduce accountability and do not implement least privilege. Option C: Trust does not replace role-based need, segregation of duties or periodic authorization review. Option D: Unused privilege remains available for accidental misuse or account compromise.
scenes.direction: Show each unsafe alternative separately with a complete, concise reason. Do not depict operational exploitation, malicious code or credential capture.

scenes.name: Defensive takeaway
scenes.visual: Use named accounts and scoped roles, remove excess privileges, segregate incompatible duties and schedule access recertification. Grant each identity only the access needed for its assigned function, and review it as roles change.
scenes.direction: Close with one readable takeaway and the next safe action. Keep the final frame long enough for comprehension.
scenes.onScreenText: Grant each identity only the access needed for its assigned function, and review it as roles change.

narration: Scenario: A data analyst has permanent administrator access to payroll, identity management and production infrastructure, although their role only requires read-only access to one reporting dataset. Safest response: Option B: Remove unnecessary privileges, grant a named read-only role for the required dataset and review access periodically. Access should be limited to the minimum necessary resources and authorizations for assigned tasks. Option A is unsafe because Shared privileged accounts reduce accountability and do not implement least privilege. Option C is unsafe because Trust does not replace role-based need, segregation of duties or periodic authorization review. Option D is unsafe because Unused privilege remains available for accidental misuse or account compromise. In practice: Use named accounts and scoped roles, remove excess privileges, segregate incompatible duties and schedule access recertification. Key takeaway: Grant each identity only the access needed for its assigned function, and review it as roles change.
